sources.name: Uniform Bar Examination Jurisdictions—MPRE Requirements - National Conference of Bar Examiners
Multistate Professional Responsibility Examination - National Conference of Bar Examiners
The Multistate Professional Responsibility Examination (MPRE) - The Bar Examiner

_: Not Required
Applicants may take the MPRE any time after completing their first year of law study.

An applicant must successfully complete the Florida General Bar Examination and the MPRE within 25 months of passing any part of the examination. If all parts are not passed within that period, older passing scores are deleted. Once all parts are passed, the scores remain vali…
The MPRE may be taken before or after the bar examination but a passing MPRE score is valid for 4 years from the date the applicant sat for that MPRE.
General Applicants must pass the MPRE within 24 months next preceding the beginning day of the written bar examination the applicant passes, or within 12 months thereafter.

The Board will accept passing MPRE scores that were obtained at any time before the applicant’s passing Virginia bar exam score expires. Passing Virginia bar exam scores expire 5 years from the date of the exam.
MPRE score must be earned no more than 3 years prior to or 40 months after the successful UBE.
Within 8 years before the successful bar examination or within 5 years after the successful bar examination or after a UBE in which the applicant earned the minimum passing score required by Arizona.

Scores are valid for 2 years from the date of administration of the MPRE; if the applicant is a licensed attorney in good standing in another US jurisdiction, an expired MPRE score of 82 or higher will satisfy the requirement.
The MPRE score report is a filing requirement and therefore it must be taken and passed prior to applying for admission.

Within 2 years before or after the date the applicant successfully takes the UBE in Indiana. For applicants admitted via transferred UBE score, no earlier than 2 years before the applicant sat for the UBE on which they achieved a score of 264.
An applicant must provide proof of a passing score within 1 year after the date of written notification of having passed the bar examination.

MPRE must have been taken within 3 years of date on which application is filed.

Acceptable MPRE score is valid for 36 months from the date of administration of the MPRE. UBE score transfer applicants must successfully complete the MPRE no earlier than 36 months before the transferred UBE score was earned.

There is no expiration date on a passing MPRE score of 80; however, a bar applicant must achieve an 80 or higher before being permitted to sit for a bar examination. An MPRE score of 75 achieved by an applicant prior to July 2017 will be accepted for admission purposes.

The applicant must either: (a) pass the MPRE within 36 months prior to applying for admission or while an application is pending; or (b) have been admitted in another jurisdiction where passage of the MPRE is required for admission and has substantially and continuously engage…
MPRE scores are valid for an unlimited period of time.
Within 4 years before or within 1 year after the date the applicant files his/her application for admission to the Connecticut Bar.

MPRE scores will not be accepted earlier than 3 years preceding the year in which an applicant passes the examination and not later than 3 years after the year in which an applicant passes the bar examination.

An MPRE for a bar exam applicant must have been taken within 3 years of the date the applicant sits for the bar exam or within 1 year after the bar exam in which the applicant obtains a passing score.

An MPRE for a bar exam applicant must have been taken within 3 years of the date the applicant sits for the bar exam or within 1 year after the bar exam in which the applicant obtains a passing score.
Within 24 months before or within 1 year after the date of administration of the Mississippi Bar Examination at which the applicant receives a passing result.

Prior to taking the Idaho Bar examination or transferring the UBE score to Idaho, or within the next two scheduled MPRE administrations after successfully completing the Idaho Bar examination or transferring the UBE score to Idaho.
MPRE scores are accepted up to 5 years from the date of release.
25 months from successful bar examination.

The MPRE must be taken and passed not earlier than 2 years before the Hawaii Bar Examination, and the MPRE score must be officially reported to the Board not later than 1 year after date of notification of passing the Hawaii Bar Examination.

An applicant for admission by examination must have taken and obtained a passing score on the MPRE within 15 years prior to the date on which the applicant is admitted. An applicant for admission by transferred Uniform Bar Examination score must have taken and obtained a passi…

No earlier than 3 years prior to the first day of the administration in which the applicant sat for the Montana Bar Examination, or no later than 9 months after successful completion of the Montana Bar Examination.

Within 4 years preceding, or by December 31 in the year after, passing the Delaware Bar Examination.
Within 28 months prior to next scheduled exam.

Not more than 8 years prior to the applicant’s Alaska application for admission.

Actual scaled score; must have attained the score within 20 months of the exam.
Accepts MBE scaled score of 133 or greater, taken within 3 years prior to the date of the exam applied for, from any jurisdiction (including Virginia).

Transferred score must have been earned within 19 months of the exam, applicant must have passed entire exam in one administration in the transferring ­jurisdiction, and applicant cannot have previously failed the Missouri exam.
A scaled score of 135 or more if taken within 37 months of present exam and part of a successful exam
